title: Infinite Queries
description: Implement infinite scrolling and load-more patterns with useInfiniteQuery.

data.text: **useInfiniteQuery** is a specialized hook for infinite scroll and load-more patterns. It manages multiple pages of data in a single cache entry, exposes fetchNextPage and hasNextPage, and handles the complexity of accumulating results across pages automatically.

Both hooks can implement pagination, but they are suited to different UX patterns. useQuery with keepPreviousData is better for traditional numbered pagination. useInfiniteQuery is better for infinite scroll and "Load More" buttons where all pages accumulate in one list.

cards.title: useQuery + keepPreviousData
cards.description: Best for traditional numbered pagination where only one page is shown at a time.
pros: Each page is a separate cache entry
cons: Only shows one page at a time
Accumulating all pages requires manual merging

cards.title: useInfiniteQuery
cards.description: Best for infinite scroll and Load More buttons where all loaded pages appear in one continuous list.
cons: All accumulated pages in memory at once

data.text: useInfiniteQuery requires three key pieces of configuration: a queryFn that accepts a pageParam, initialPageParam to set the starting page, and getNextPageParam to tell React Query when there are more pages to load.

data.title: Basic useInfiniteQuery
initialPageParam is Required in v5
data.text: React Query v5 requires initialPageParam to be explicitly set. The first call to queryFn receives this value. Set it to null, '', 0, or 1 depending on your API's expected page parameter format.

data.text: useInfiniteQuery works with both cursor-based (token/string) and offset-based (page number) APIs. For offset-based pagination, pass the page number as pageParam and increment it in getNextPageParam.

data.title: Build an Infinite Image Gallery
data.description: Create an infinite-scrolling image gallery using useInfiniteQuery. Each 'page' from the API returns 8 images with a nextCursor. Implement the gallery with a Load More button.
steps: Create a mock API fetchImagePage(cursor) that returns 8 images, a title, and a nextCursor (null on the last page)
Create a function generateImage(id) to create consistent mock image objects
Create an InfiniteImageGallery component using useInfiniteQuery
Set initialPageParam to null and use cursor-based pagination
Render images in a responsive CSS grid using Tailwind (grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4)
Show a 'Load More' button disabled when !hasNextPage or isFetchingNextPage
Show a 'You've seen all images!' message when !hasNextPage and data exists
Add a fade-in animation for newly loaded images
data.expectedOutcome: A responsive image gallery that loads 8 images per click, accumulates all loaded images in one scrollable grid, shows loading and end states correctly, and never makes duplicate page requests.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useInfiniteQuery manages multiple pages of data in a single cache entry
data.pages is an array of all successfully fetched page results
initialPageParam is required in v5 and sets the starting page parameter
getNextPageParam returns the next page param or undefined when there are no more pages
fetchNextPage loads the next page; hasNextPage tells you if more pages exist
Use useInfiniteQuery for infinite scroll and Load More; use useQuery for numbered pagination
Cursor-based APIs pass strings; offset-based APIs pass numbers as pageParam
data.takeaway: useInfiniteQuery turns the complexity of accumulating paginated data into a simple hook with two functions: fetchNextPage and hasNextPage.
